invocation_id_provenance: read from the unit's own `InvocationID` property at launch (12:35:35Z) and again at 13:56:49Z, WHILE LoadState=loaded. It cannot be read now: the unit was launched under heavy_run_form v1, without `RemainAfterExit=yes`, so it was COLLECTED at exit

journal_copy.counts_note: they differ legitimately when the NAME has been used more than once; the id is the run
journal_copy.cross_check: the by-id count against `-u <unit>`; a unit NAME names every run ever launched under it, an id names ONE
journal_copy.field_not_used_here: INVOCATION_ID -- the SYSTEM manager's field; it matches nothing under --user
fields_matched: USER_INVOCATION_ID (the user manager's lines: Started, Consumed, Failed)
journal_copy.how_that_is_computed: the run's own `Started` line is still present, so this copy reaches the beginning of the run. False means the beginning has already rotated -- which happened to DE 84's within four hours
lines: 2026-09-06T14:01:55.605081+00:00 ip-172-31-78-41 systemd[1004]: de95smoke.service: Consumed 1h 26min 12.243s CPU time, 2.3G memory peak, 0B memory swap peak.

retention.it_is_a_MEASUREMENT_not_a_property: five reads across one hour walked the window's start from 08:45Z to 09:29:57Z -- about as fast as the clock. A retention state named once is stale within minutes, so it carries its own as-of and query (R-646 R4)
retention.oldest_entry_from: the entry's OWN clock, as journald printed it -- never typed, never a policy setting
retention.query: journalctl --user --no-pager -o short-iso-precise (first line = the oldest entry retained)

the_coordinators_earlier_copy.why_both: the coordinator copied the Started line at 13:39Z, while the run was live; this copies what the journal holds for the same invocation at the run's END. Two reads of a rotating store at two moments, each with its own as-of

the_unit_reading_after_exit_is_VOID.why: LoadState is `not-found`: the unit was collected and every field above is a DEFAULT. `ExecMainStatus=0` and `Result=success` here are NOT this run's outcome and are not quoted as one. The RECEIPT is the record

why_this_sidecar_exists: the sealed receipt's producing code predates DE 96, so it cannot carry its own launch record. Rule 20 as amended (R-641): the journal is NOT the record -- a number read from it is copied into an artifact at the moment of reading with the source's retention state named
